q-343875.name: Question 1
q-343875.problem:
Select the missing parts in a particular solution of the differential equation ${y}^{″}+9y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $4$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

*Hint: You may assume that the free term and all the cosine coefficients in the Fourier series of the particular solution are equal to zero.*

The Fourier series of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-1}}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})
$$
q-343875.worked_solution:
We assume that a solution of our equation has the following Fourier series:

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, we compute the derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\ {y}_{p}^{″} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{b}_{n}{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{p}^{″}$ and ${y}_{p}$ into the equation:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{b}_{n}{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})+9({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Rearranging the terms to find a common denominator:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}(9-\frac{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})
$$

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}(\frac{36-{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, equating the sine coefficients:

$$
\frac{{b}_{n}(36-{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2})}{4}=\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi }\,⇒\,{b}_{n}=\frac{8(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi (36-{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2})}.
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{8(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}\pi (36-{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2})}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

q-343882.name: Question 2
q-343882.problem:
Select the missing parts in a particular solution of the differential equation ${y}^{″}-5y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $4$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x)∼5+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

*Hint: You may assume that all the cosine coefficients in the Fourier series of the particular solution are equal to zero.*

The Fourier series of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{{field-1}}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-2}}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})
$$
q-343882.worked_solution:
We assume that a solution of our equation has the following Fourier series:

$$
{y}_{p}∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, we compute the derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\ {y}_{p}^{″} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{b}_{n}{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{p}^{″}$ and ${y}_{p}$ into the equation and have

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{b}_{n}{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})-5(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))=5+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Rearranging the terms, we get 

$$
-5\cdot \frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}(-\frac{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}-5)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})=5+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, equating the free terms and sine coefficients, we obtain:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-5\cdot \frac{{a}_{0}}{2}=5 \\ {b}_{n}(-\frac{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}-5)=\frac{2(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\end{aligned}\,⇒\,\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}=-1 \\ {b}_{n}=-\frac{8(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+20)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼-1+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,-\frac{8(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+20)}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

q-343886.problem:
Select the missing parts in a particular solution of the differential equation ${y}^{″}-10y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $4$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x)∼10+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{5(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

*Hint: You may assume that all the cosine coefficients in the Fourier series of the particular solution are equal to zero.*

The Fourier series of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{{field-1}}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-2}}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})
$$
q-343886.worked_solution:
We assume that a solution of our equation has the following Fourier series:

$$
{y}_{p}∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, we compute the derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\ {y}_{p}^{″} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{b}_{n}{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{p}^{″}$ and ${y}_{p}$ into the equation and have

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{b}_{n}{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})-10(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))=10+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{5(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Rearranging the terms, we get 

$$
-10\cdot \frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}(-\frac{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}-10)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})=10+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{5(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, equating the free terms and sine coefficients, we obtain:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-10\cdot \frac{{a}_{0}}{2}=10 \\ {b}_{n}(-\frac{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}-10)=\frac{5(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\end{aligned}\,⇒\,\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}=-1 \\ {b}_{n}=\frac{20(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+40)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼-1+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{20(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+40)}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

q-343887.name: Question 4
q-343887.problem:
Consider the differential equation ${y}^{″}+\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4}y=f(x),$ where the $4$-periodic forcing function is given by 

$$
f(x)∼2+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Select the correct options in the reasoning below regarding the resonant component of a particular solution of the equation.

The natural frequency of the system matches the frequency of the {{field-1}} harmonic of the forcing function. 

Consequently, the particular solution contains a resonant term of the form

$$
{y}_{{p}_{3}}={{field-2}}.
$$
q-343887.worked_solution:
We begin by identifying resonance. The differential equation 

$$
{y}^{″}+\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4}y=f(x)
$$

has a natural frequency of 

$$
\omega =\sqrt{\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4}}=\frac{3\pi }{2}.
$$

The frequencies of the forcing harmonics for a $4$-periodic function $(L=2)$ are 

$$
{\omega }_{n}=\frac{n\pi }{2}.
$$

For $n=3$, we have ${\omega }_{3}=\frac{3\pi }{2}.$ Since ${\omega }_{3}=\omega ,$ the $n=3$ harmonic of the forcing function causes resonance.

For the $n=3$ harmonic, the forcing term is 

$$
{f}_{3}(x)=\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2}).
$$

Because this frequency matches the natural frequency, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{{p}_{3}}=x(A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})).
$$

Now, we compute the derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{{p}_{3}}^{′} & =(A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2}))+x(-\frac{3\pi }{2}A\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})+\frac{3\pi }{2}B\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})) \\ {y}_{{p}_{3}}^{″} & =-3\pi A\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})+3\pi B\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})-\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4}x(A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2}))\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{{p}_{3}}^{″}$ and ${y}_{{p}_{3}}$ into the equation ${y}^{″}+\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4}y=\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2}):$

$$
[-3\pi A\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})+3\pi B\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})-\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4}{y}_{{p}_{3}}]+\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{4}{y}_{{p}_{3}}=\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})
$$

The resonant terms involving $x$ cancel out, leaving

$$
-3\pi A\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})+3\pi B\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2})=\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, equating the sine and cosine coefficients, we obtain:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3\pi A=0 \\ 3\pi B=\frac{1}{9}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,\{\begin{aligned}A=0 \\ B=\frac{1}{27\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resonant component of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{{p}_{3}}=\frac{x}{27\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi x}{2}).
$$
